描述_ZN: Green-glazed, incised, single-handled jug, Northern dynasty, 21.3 cm high, mouth 11 cm in diameter, foot 12 cm in diameter, the mouth of the jug with a rim, short neck, sloping shoulders, and bulging belly, supported by a solid pie-shaped foot. The vertical tether is symmetrically placed on both sides of the shoulder, with a short tubular stream on the other side and a curved handle on the side opposite the stream. The form is full and rounded. The body is heavy and off-white. Inside and outside the pot are glazed, glaze green, glaze layer transparent, glaze glass feeling is strong, glaze open fine fragment pattern.　　The entire body of the pot is decorated with incised flowers, and the decoration is divided into three layers, with the shoulders and the lower part of the belly with the supine and overlapping lotus petal patterns respectively, and with the lingzhi pattern between the supine and overlapping lotus petal patterns, separated by the string pattern between the patterns. The pattern is clearly layered and skillfully decorated.　　After Buddhism was introduced to China in the Eastern Han Dynasty, it tended to flourish during the Northern and Southern Dynasties, which was reflected in the decoration of porcelain, where lotus, lotus petal, and lonicera motifs were very popular, with distinctive features of the period.　　This object was donated by Mr. Chen Wanli, a researcher at the National Palace Museum and a world-renowned ceramic expert in modern times. The ceramics donated by Mr. Chen have enriched the collection of the National Palace Museum, and some of the objects are preferred exhibits in successive ceramic displays at the National Palace Museum.
